record.title: DolphinBench evaluates agent memory through task completion, cost and latency
record.summary: A September 2026 paper introduces DolphinBench, a benchmark for testing agent memory through completion of knowledge-work tasks that depend on long conversation histories. The abstract describes three personas with roughly 500k tokens of messages each and 200 tasks per persona; each task is checked by comparing an agent run with and without the relevant history. The authors require reports of total cost and latency alongside accuracy. This is a paper-reported benchmark design, not evidence that any memory system performs better; the full protocol and independent validation were not inspected in this activation.

Performance on real and diverse histories and across independently evaluated memory systems has not been established.

brief.importance_rationale: If valid and adopted, measuring task completion alongside cost and latency can change memory-system selection and expose quality-efficiency tradeoffs. Score 4 reflects a useful evaluation contribution; broad validity and adoption are not established.
limitations: This activation inspected the arXiv abstract only; full protocol and artifact were not inspected.
The abstract does not establish task diversity, persona realism, annotation reliability or independent validity.
No comparative result for any memory system is claimed here.
Generalization beyond three knowledge-work personas and the stated histories is unknown.

The abstract describes three personas with roughly 500k tokens of messages each and 200 tasks per persona; each task is checked by comparing an agent run with and without the relevant history. The authors require reports of total cost and latency alongside accuracy. This is a paper-reported benchmark design, not evidence that any memory system performs better; the full protocol and independent validation were not inspected in this activation.

technical.claimed_result: The paper describes three personas with about 500k tokens each and 200 tasks per persona, with task relevance checked through with-history versus without-history runs.
technical.demonstrated_result: The abstract and its stated benchmark design are directly inspectable. No comparative performance result or benchmark reproduction was established in this activation.
technical.mechanism: The benchmark tests memory through agent task completion on information embedded in long histories. Each task is intended to depend on that history, checked by success with relevant history and failure without it; submissions report accuracy, total cost and latency.
technical.novelty: The benchmark centers task completion and requires cost and latency reporting alongside accuracy, rather than relying only on cued retrieval questions.
technical.regime: Three knowledge-work personas and 200 tasks per persona over long message histories; abstract-level description only. Generalization to real users, other domains and non-synthetic histories is unknown.
technical.reproducibility: The arXiv abstract is accessible; the full task-generation protocol, released artifact and independent reproduction were not checked.
technical.strongest_baseline: The stated within-task control compares the same task with and without its relevant history. The abstract does not report comparative results across memory systems.

brief.title: DolphinBench evaluates agent memory through task completion, cost and latency
brief.why_it_matters: If the benchmark's task construction and controls are valid, evaluating task success, cost and latency together could expose memory-system tradeoffs hidden by cued question-answer accuracy alone. The abstract supports the existence and stated design of a new benchmark, but does not establish that its tasks generalize beyond three synthetic knowledge-work personas or that any system has a favorable frontier.
